extraction_text: Nothing in this section shall be construed so as to prevent the Publisher from requiring the use of more efficient or less expensive processes than presently in use in its plant, however, no such change in process will be made which will deprive Composing Room employees of the Employer to do in its plant for production of display advertising copy for the newspapers, as the kind of copy is defined in this section and other than two-column classified display ads, and provided that other employees of the Publisher may type or otherwise produce copy by typewriter or otherwise prior to Composing Room use thereof in connection with any necessary keystroking in the Composing Room.

3-01 In the event of the introduction of new equipment, or processes to perform work within the jurisdiction of the union the employer will provide training on said equipment or processes. None but employees, as defined in the contract, shall be permitted to work on any such process or equipment except as provided elsewhere in this agreement.

No one other than the Employer has any right to determine what processes, machinery and equipment are to be installed and used in the Employer's plant, such determination being the sole prerogative of the Employer.

Notwithstanding any other provision in this Agreement (including Section 54-01), the Employer reserves the right to assign the following work to persons inside or outside the bargaining unit: (1) Electronic and/or computer marking of display advertising, classified advertising, news and editorial copy and legal matter; (2) Inputting of text and graphics into electronic and/or computer systems for display advertising, classified advertising, news and editorial copy and legal matter; and (3) Electronic and/or computer makeup (building) of display advertising, classified advertising, news and editorial copy and legal matter.

42-01 Tape punching machines, scanners and other equipment in the Composing Room shall be operated or monitored by Composing Room personnel as in the past so long as such equipment is used in Composing Room operations.

53-01 Notwithstanding any other provision of this agreement, it is agreed that if a computer, or other equipment used in typesetting is performing Composing Room work within the jurisdiction of the Union, the jurisdiction of the Union includes the operation of the computer and such other equipment used in typesetting, programming (except programming which the Employer may have done by the manufacturer of the equipment or by personnel similar to a manufacturer's programming personnel or by not more than one employee of the Publisher not a member of the Union), and maintenance of such equipment in the Composing Room (except when the Employer determines it is necessary to have maintenance work performed by outside technicians); and it is further agreed that the Employer has the right to install, operate and use devices in its Editorial and Advertising Departments for the production of copy and editing of such copy, and the employees in the bargaining unit will accept and process all such copy, as well as copy received by the Employer from or by means of the Associated Press or United Press International (including syndicate copy which may be received via a wire service facility), or a substitute for either of them, in whatever form any such copy is received, as may be required by the Employer, and no rekeyboarding or reproduction of any such copy in the Composing Room will be required. The Employer may also install direct input devices in the Composing Room to be used by Composing Room personnel.

At least one employee employed by the Employer will be present if possible for assistance and observation whenever any technicians outside the bargaining unit do maintenance work on any such equipment in the Composing Room.

Scanner ready copy and electronic impulses produced and received by the Editorial Departments will be accepted and processed by Composing Room employees. Copy received by the Editorial Departments from outside sources (not produced by Editorial Department employees) which is not scanner ready, or camera ready, or which is not in the form of electronic impulses will be perforated or otherwise prepared for input into the Publisher's system by Composing room personnel.

Personnel in the Publisher's Editorial Departments may use terminals to directly input material for typesetting to the Publisher's computer system. The Editorial Departments may utilize terminals to recall scanner prepared or directly input material from electronic storage to make editorial changes.

The publisher will not create or establish typing pools in its Editorial Departments for the purposes of preparing copy for the computer system. It is understood, of course, that regular employees in the Editorial Departments may use typewriters in the preparation and editing of copy for scanners and may use terminals, typewriters and other devices to directly input copy into the editorial and computer systems.

Wire services (AP, UPI or substitutes for either), and syndicated and feature copy that is received by or for the Editorial Departments in tape or equivalent process, scanner ready, camera ready or as electronic impulses, will be accepted in original and edited form and processed by Composing Room employees.

Personnel in the Publisher's Classified department may use terminals to directly input classified ad material for typesetting into the Employer's computer system. Scanner ready copy or copy produced by electronic impulses from the Classified Department, with respect to classified ads, as herein defined including classified display ads of two (2) columns in width, will be accepted and processed in the Composing Room. Rules, borders, logos and illustrations that are included which are capable of being done by the computer system of the Publisher may be used as produced by the typesetting system.
The Advertising Department may utilize terminals to recall classified ads from electronic storage in order to add to, delete or kill copy and also for the addition of necessary coding.

All display ad copy other than two (2) column classified display and legals in excess of two (2) columns, which is keyboarded in the Publisher's plant, will be performed by Composing Room employees provided, however that display ads or parts thereof ready or substantially ready for camera or which are received partially complete for camera shall be processed by Composing Room employees, as in the past. However, the key stroking necessary to be done in the Employer's plant to produce classified display ads in excess of two (2) columns will be done by Composing Room employees.

It is recognized that this contract differs from certain previous agreements between the parties in that it includes provisions for specific additional benefits in lieu of previous contract provisions which required the reproduction of local advertisements and other matter received from sources outside the composing room. It is understood and agreed that the Employer has a right to use such material without subsequent reproduction of such work by employees covered by this agreement. It is further agreed that the Employer shall not subcontract work when it has the necessary equipment and its employees possess the necessary skills to perform the work. The Employer shall have no liability or responsibility hereafter to reproduce or reset any matter of any kind, whether originally published prior to the effective date of this agreement or after such effective date.

It is further recognized that the contract provisions requiring all work within the jurisdiction of the Union to be performed only by employees covered by this agreement is not applicable to the work referred to in this section.

Subject to the provisions hereof and the jurisdictional rights, if any, of any other Union with which the Employer has had contracts in the past, Composing Room employees shall do ordinary adjustment and maintenance work on terminal equipment which may be situated in Employer's Advertising and Editorial Departments.

Only Composing Room employees will operate terminals or other equipment, if directed by the employer, to do the key stroking which may be necessary to be performed by employees of the Publisher for typesetting of display ads, except as hereinabove noted (in Paragraph 56-05 above).

There shall be no abridgement of the right to utilization of terminals and computers or other devices of like purpose by the Publisher, by persons employed by the Publisher outside the bargaining unit, for purposes other than Composing Room work.
